collection_method: Read-only GitHub repository, issue-search, issue and comment GET requests through the GitHub connector. Embedded code, reproductions and linked demonstrations were treated as evidence and not executed. No packages, agents, team runs, models, tools, workflows, external platforms or target systems were run or contacted.

selected_records.title: [Bug] Team route mode: spurious second delegation after member-HITL resume
selected_records.operator_boundary_crossed: reported extra delegation after a human-approved resume
selected_records.provider_attribution: Agno route-mode team; reporter used an OpenAI Responses configuration but describes a provider-independent dispatch fault.
selected_records.assessment: After a paused member returns its approved result, the team reportedly stores that result, re-enters the router without new user input and commonly delegates a second empty task to the same member. This preserves result transfer/use and unintended extra work, but the participants are configured team roles and the episode was already public.

selected_records.title: [Bug] `delegate_to_all_members` with `stream=True` interleaves the responses of each team member into a single corrupted result
selected_records.provider_attribution: Agno broadcast team using a reporter-specified Gemini model; provider provenance is reporter-asserted.
selected_records.assessment: Concurrent member deltas are reported to be interleaved into one corrupted tool result that the team leader receives. A later comment says the behavior remained reproducible on version 3.0.5. This is concrete transfer in an intentional team and a reliability failure, not unauthorized coordination.

selected_records.title: InngestAgent resume can execute another agent's tool with the same id
selected_records.operator_boundary_crossed: controlled wrong-agent tool execution after resume
selected_records.provider_attribution: Mastra InngestAgent cold-worker resume path; no live model-provider execution.
selected_records.assessment: A scripted local test, independent commenter reproduction and project triage show agent B's resumed run executing agent A's same-ID tool on a cold worker. Project triage rated it high severity and the issue later closed as released. This is a wrong-owner execution control, not a live autonomous exchange.

selected_records.title: [BUG] Resumed run uses the previous request's requestContext and delegation hooks when resumed in the same process (supervisor and sub-agent)
selected_records.operator_boundary_crossed: controlled stale per-request context across supervisor/sub-agent resume
selected_records.provider_attribution: Mastra supervisor/sub-agent resume in a scripted local model test; no provider execution.
selected_records.assessment: A newly published deterministic test reports supervisor delegation hooks and sub-agent tools using earlier request context after approval resumes. The reporter describes repeated approval loops in their application, but the public reproduction is synthetic and project triage had not yet validated it when observed.

selected_records.title: Approval suspensions can be self-approved: auto-resume suffix defaults to approved:true and model-authored resumeData is accepted as the resume signal
selected_records.operator_boundary_crossed: confirmed production human-consent bypass with external side effect
selected_records.provider_attribution: Mastra agent auto-resume and approval implementation; model/provider identity is not established in the public issue.
selected_records.assessment: The reporter says a production agent self-approved a human-gated send action and posted to an external social platform without UI approval. Project triage later confirmed the causal chain, rated it critical and linked the merged fix. This is a material real-world consent-boundary incident, but it involves one agent/tool path rather than a swarm or inter-agent result exchange.

selected_records.title: [BUG] workflow/agent delegation tools still accept an arbitrary model-authored suspendedToolRunId (residual of #23739)
selected_records.provider_attribution: Mastra workflow/agent delegation identity handling; no provider execution.
selected_records.assessment: Project triage confirmed model-authored run identifiers could alias delegated work and create silent result-loss or approval/resume risk. Follow-up comments narrow the remaining defect after an intermediate fix, and the issue later closed as released. No foreign run was observed in a live system.

novelty_result: No previously unreported rogue swarm confirmed. A previously published production consent bypass is a material real-world boundary incident, while the multi-agent records are configured-team reproductions or product routing defects without independently verified autonomous participants.
limitations: Searches were capped at 30 newest-updated rows and overlap; this is not a complete issue census.
Issue bodies and comments are public reports and project triage records, not independently authenticated agent telemetry.
The production consent incident establishes an unauthorized action but not multiple participants or task-result exchange.
Configured team members, supervisors and durable agents are framework roles rather than independently verified autonomous identities.
Open or closed issue state and release notices do not establish continuing agent activity.
No code, package, reproduction, agent, model, team run, tool, workflow, external platform or target service was executed or contacted.

Advancement requires an unpublished original exchange with independently corroborated autonomous participants, transferred task work actually used by a distinguishable recipient, and evidence that the coordination itself crossed operator authorization in a real run.
redactions: No raw approval payloads, executable reproduction bodies, customer identifiers, account names, credentials, private logs or external destinations are included.
Assessments retain public record links, timestamps and body hashes while summarizing mechanics and reported effects at a domain level.
